baseline_models.focus_anchor: The three لَئِنْ clauses move through أُخْرِجُوا / قُوتِلُوا / نَصَرُوهُمْ and end with ثُمَّ لَا يُنصَرُونَ.
baseline_models.mechanism: The conditions form an escalating audit of coalition capacity: accompany partners through forced removal, enter reciprocal combat for them, then sustain any attempted intervention. Each higher demand exposes a deeper failure, from refusing shared movement to abandoning the field and losing rescue altogether.

activation_trace.role: Passage from a settled place to its outside supplies the first, spatial test of whether the allies will share displacement.
Reciprocal fighting between parties raises the test from accompanying movement to exposed participation in conflict.
Aid that makes another prevail is repeatedly proposed, denied, briefly conceded, and finally denied in the passive.
Turning away converts even the conceded act of aid into withdrawal.
Showing the back in battle gives the coalition audit its visible terminal failure.

changed_reading.before: The ayah merely predicts that unreliable allies will act cowardly.
changed_reading.after: The ayah runs a graduated stress test: shared place, shared danger, sustained aid, and access to rescue fail in sequence, exposing a coalition that cannot carry commitment across stages.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The hinge نَّصَرُوهُمْ لَيُوَلُّنَّ ٱلْأَدْبَارَ places aid directly beside emphatic back-turning.
baseline_models.mechanism: The root field of و ل ي contains both supportive affiliation and withdrawal. The construction activates that internal reversal: apparent protective nearness becomes physical and social distancing, while أَدْبَار turns the relation into mutually exposed backs.

activation_trace.role: Mutual aid supplies the supportive relation that the next verb overturns.
The root's affiliation, love, and support image supplies the latent bond being tested.
The realized sense of turning away reverses affiliation into abandonment.
People presenting backs to one another turns battlefield retreat into mutual estrangement.

changed_reading.before: Turning their backs is only a report of retreat after entering battle.
changed_reading.after: The retreat is the semantic inversion of alliance itself: the claimed relation of protective nearness changes into reciprocal back-facing and severance.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: ن ص ر occurs three times, moving from active non-aid to hypothetical active aid and then passive non-rescue.
baseline_models.mechanism: The repeated root rotates helper, beneficiary, and passive patient without establishing a durable source of support. The final passive leaves the plural referent open enough that aider and aided converge in one unsupported horizon: horizontal promises circulate, but no backstop remains when the chain is tested.

activation_trace.role: Aid and being made to prevail rotate through active and passive forms, exposing a support chain with no stable guarantor.
One thing following another without interruption supplies the expected continuity that the retreat breaks.
The rear or terminal phase makes ثُمَّ لَا يُنصَرُونَ the outcome of a broken relay rather than another isolated denial.

changed_reading.before: The repeated ن ص ر simply emphasizes that no help will be available.
changed_reading.after: The repetitions diagram a failed relay: aid may be announced or even initiated, but role rotation and retreat leave every participant without a final source of rescue.

context_deltas.mechanism: 59:11 supplies a first-person pledge built from the same ordered acts that 59:12 negates. The focus ayah is therefore not only a forecast of weakness; it is a clause-by-clause performance audit in which verbal brotherhood is replayed as non-accompaniment, non-aid, and emphatic retreat.

activation_trace.role: Saying what does not become fact frames the pledge as speech awaiting a performance test.
Brotherhood and kinship name the relation whose practical obligations are being claimed.
The paired promise of expulsion and accompanying exit supplies the first clause copied into the audit.
Reciprocal combat supplies the second promised contingency.
The emphatic promise of aid supplies the commitment that 59:12 first denies and then stress-tests.
Knowledge-bearing testimony turns the repeated scenario into an evidentiary judgment.
The explicit opposite of truth supplies the verdict that the next ayah demonstrates structurally.
The focus repeats the exit contingency but removes the promised accompaniment.
The focus repeats the combat contingency as the second failed test.
Repeated aid language converts one emphatic pledge into denial, concession, collapse, and final non-rescue.
Emphatic turning away supplies the behavior that falsifies the promise.
The displayed backs make failure publicly legible rather than merely inward.

structural_cues: 59:11 and 59:12 preserve the sequence خ ر ج ثم ق ت ل ثم ن ص ر.
First-person emphatic promises in 59:11 are answered by third-person negations and an emphatic retreat in 59:12.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated verb chain and the testimony/lie frame; I infer that repetition functions as a performative audit, while the live alternative is that 59:12 is only a prediction appended to the verdict.

changed_reading.before: The focus independently predicts what the allies would do under pressure.
changed_reading.after: The focus quotes the pledge back in behavioral form: every promised obligation is matched by its failure, so syntax itself demonstrates the lie.

context_deltas.mechanism: 59:8 joins actual expulsion to active support and labels the actors truthful; 59:9 adds choosing others over oneself despite privation. Against that cost-bearing pattern, the focus ayah's refusal to leave and sustain aid becomes a negative definition of solidarity: affiliation is true only when it transfers place, risk, and scarce capacity into action.

activation_trace.role: Actual forced passage outside one's home supplies embodied displacement rather than a merely verbal contingency.
Active aid under displacement supplies a positive comparator for the focus's repeated failures of aid.
Fulfilling a claim through action makes performed commitment the local measure of truth.
Choosing another over oneself supplies the costly allocation that real solidarity can require.
Refusal to share outward movement fails the earlier cost-bearing comparator.
The aid root's repeated collapse marks the absence of performed commitment.

structural_cues: 59:8 places expulsion, aid, and the label الصادقون in one sequence.
59:9 immediately renders solidarity as preference for others despite one's own need, while 59:11 later labels unsupported promises كاذبون.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the lexical contrast and adjacent cost-bearing action; I infer that willingness to absorb displacement and scarcity is a local test of solidarity, though the earlier acts have broader objects and are not grammatical co-referents of 59:12.

changed_reading.before: The ayah condemns one group's cowardice in an isolated military alliance.
changed_reading.after: The ayah is the negative panel of a surah-level solidarity test: claims are measured by whether partners actually share displacement, danger, and scarce capacity.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surrounding material distinguishes external enclosure from internal cohesion. Fortresses and walls can gather bodies behind a boundary, but the explicitly scattered hearts cannot sustain mobile mutual aid; the focus's back-turning is the battlefield manifestation of a coalition already divided within.

activation_trace.role: Protection inside an enclosing fort supplies the earlier mistaken substitute for effective support.
Gathering dispersed parts into one body names the unity that appears present from outside.
The fortified settlement encloses combatants physically without proving relational cohesion.
The raised wall supplies a hard external boundary behind which apparent unity can be staged.
Inner dispersion directly negates the gathering image and explains why collective action breaks.
Turning away turns concealed inner separation into outward motion.
Back-turning makes the coalition's fracture visible on the field.
Failed aid is the functional consequence of enclosure without cohesion.

structural_cues: حصون in 59:2 and محصنة plus جدر in 59:14 bracket the focus with repeated enclosure imagery.
59:14 repeats جميعا but opposes that appearance with قلوبهم شتى.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies fortification, apparent gathering, and scattered hearts; I infer that retreat reveals pre-existing social fragmentation, while the live alternative is that walls and retreat remain only tactical descriptions.

changed_reading.before: They turn their backs because the battle goes badly.
changed_reading.after: Their retreat reveals that walls had gathered bodies but never integrated the coalition; the outward flight is an inner scattering becoming visible.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later parable supplies a social sequence in which speech induces another's risky commitment and is followed by declared separation when consequences arrive. That sequence sharpens the focus's move from promised aid to retreat: the alliance can function as risk transfer, not merely failed courage.

activation_trace.role: A formally presented parable authorizes comparison of the later action sequence with the focus's alliance sequence.
Two spoken acts bracket the other's compliance: inducement first and distancing speech afterward.
Declared innocence and separation supplies the disowning phase after risk has been externalized.
Anticipation of harm supplies the stated motive under which the instigator withdraws.
Promised or attempted aid supplies the initial affiliative posture.
Turning away supplies the withdrawal phase after commitment has become costly.
Mutual back-facing makes withdrawal a severed social relation, not only a change of direction.

structural_cues: 59:16 places the other's compliance between an inducing command and a declaration of disavowal.
59:12 likewise moves from the possibility of aid to emphatic withdrawal once aid entails exposure.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a marked parable, paired speech acts, disavowal, and fear; I infer a shared inducement-to-abandonment mechanism, while the parable may also describe a broader relation rather than identifying only the speakers of 59:11.

changed_reading.before: The allies make a sincere attempt but flee when courage fails.
changed_reading.after: The alliance may be a mechanism for transferring risk: speech draws partners into exposure, then the promiser severs affiliation when consequences arrive.

context_deltas.mechanism: The rear/end range of أَدْبَار, the sequencing force of ثُمَّ, and the later dual outcome shift attention from the instant of flight to what follows it. Retreat does not establish a safe outside for the abandoning party; it begins an aftermath in which the attempted helper and the abandoned partner can converge in non-rescue and consequence.

activation_trace.role: An example functioning as warning directs the reader from the immediate scene toward repeatable consequence.
The end and outcome of a matter supplies the later temporal horizon shared by both parties.
The back as the last or receding part converts spatial flight into the opening of an aftermath.
Final passive non-rescue supplies the state into which the participants may converge after retreat.

structural_cues: ثُمَّ delays the last non-rescue beyond the moment of back-turning.
59:17 uses the dual عاقبتهما, keeping instigator and induced party together in the stated outcome.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies end/outcome language, delayed sequencing, and a dual result; I infer that escape fails to separate the deserter's fate from the abandoned party's, while the final passive plural in 59:12 remains referentially open.

changed_reading.before: One party escapes by retreating while the abandoned party alone remains without help.
changed_reading.after: Back-turning opens rather than ends the consequence: abandonment does not secure an independent refuge, and the relation collapses toward a shared unrescued aftermath.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it maps a social pledge onto the packet's tunnel architecture for ن ف ق. It remains anchored in the focus's doubled خ ر ج and emphatic و ل ي / د ب ر movement, but downstream prose should present it as an exploratory spatial analogy, not as a lexical derivation or exhaustive definition of hypocrisy.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus begins with two forms of خ ر ج and culminates in an emphatic turn of the backs.

activation_trace.role: Showing one entrance while concealing an exit supplies an architectural image for public commitment paired with reserved escape.
Movement to the outside makes exit behavior the first explicit test of the concealed route.
Turning away activates the reserved outlet when exposure rises.
Visible backs reveal the direction of the previously concealed exit.

changed_reading.before: The speakers lie and later flee.
changed_reading.after: The alliance behaves like a two-opening structure: a public entrance advertises brotherhood, while a concealed exit is reserved for the moment commitment becomes costly.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is a cross-domain activation from aid into hydrology: ن ص ر can image beneficent rain and remote channels, while nearby وَبَال can image heavy rain. The repeated focus root and the explicit context branch keep it packet-anchored, but prose should mark it as a material analogy rather than claim literal weather or replace the military-social reading.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus repeats ن ص ر three times and closes by withholding its passive result.

activation_trace.role: Rain as relief turns expected aid into a life-giving supply that never arrives.
Channels arriving from afar at pooled water model a distributed support network whose links fail under pressure.
Experiencing and testing a thing makes the network's failure something materially undergone.
Heavy rain reverses the absent beneficent rain of aid into an injurious deluge of consequence.

changed_reading.before: No military assistance reaches the threatened group.
changed_reading.after: The coalition resembles a failed watershed: channels promise relief but transmit no sustaining flow, and the nearby consequence converts hoped-for rescue-rain into a heavy, harmful downpour.

strongest_changes: The exact verb order in 59:11 turns 59:12 into a performative audit of a pledge, not an independent assertion of cowardice.
59:8-9 calibrate truthful solidarity as cost-bearing action, so refusal to share displacement and risk becomes the focus's central ethical failure.
Fortification and apparent gathering cannot compensate for scattered hearts; retreat externalizes an already fragmented coalition.
The later induce-then-disown parable exposes alliance speech as a possible mechanism for transferring risk before withdrawal.
summary.what_was_special: The focus compresses an entire alliance failure into repeated roots and grammatical role changes: promised exit and aid are replayed as negation, affiliation flips into back-turning, and active helping ends in passive non-rescue.
remaining_uncertainties: The referent of the final passive plural remains open, so the shared-aftermath model is stronger as a convergence reading than as a fixed pronoun resolution.
The costly-solidarity contrast is contextual and ethical rather than direct grammatical co-reference.
The hidden-exit and rain-reversal readings are deliberately branch-distant analogies and should remain explicitly exploratory.
